characters.description: The heir of Gondor's ancient kings, now moving openly toward his birthright. He takes a perilous hidden road to gather strength for the war and to come to the aid of the besieged white city in its darkest hour.
characters.name: Aragorn

characters.description: The white wizard, now the chief mover of the free peoples against the Enemy, who rides to the great city of Gondor with Pippin to help ready its defense against the coming storm.
characters.name: Gandalf

characters.description: The young hobbit, carried to Gondor by Gandalf, who out of gratitude enters the service of the city's Steward and soon finds himself caught up in the siege of Minas Tirith.
characters.name: Peregrin Took

characters.description: The proud Steward who rules Gondor in the absence of a king - wise and commanding, but stern and sinking into despair. Grief for his sons and a secret dread gnaw at his will as the enemy's armies close in around his city.
characters.name: Denethor

characters.description: The king of Rohan, restored to vigor, who answers Gondor's call for aid and gathers his riders to ride to the great battle far to the south.
characters.name: Théoden

characters.description: A noblewoman of Rohan, the king's niece, brave and chafing at being left behind to keep house while the men ride to war. Longing for a share in the danger, she rides secretly to battle in disguise among the soldiers.
characters.name: Éowyn

characters.description: The hobbit left in Rohan's keeping, likewise forbidden the ride to battle, who is carried along in secret and refuses to abandon his king when the fighting comes.
characters.name: Meriadoc Brandybuck

characters.description: The dread chief of the Enemy's ringwraiths, a lord of terror who commands the assault on Gondor. It is said no living man can bring him down, and his very presence saps the courage of those who face him.
characters.name: The Witch-king

characters.description: The Ring-bearer, a prisoner in the enemy's tower as the final stretch of the quest begins, his strength nearly spent by the burden he still carries toward the Mountain of Fire.
characters.name: Frodo Baggins

characters.description: Frodo's faithful servant, who braves the enemy's tower to rescue his master and bears him - and for a time the ring itself - onward across the ashen wastes of Mordor toward their goal.
characters.name: Samwise Gamgee

recaps.ending: The Return of the King closes with the war won and the world remade. The One Ring is destroyed in Mount Doom, undone at the last not by Frodo, whose will failed, but by Gollum, who seized it and fell into the fire, and Sauron's power is broken forever, his armies scattered and his strongholds thrown down. Aragorn is crowned King Elessar, reuniting the realms of Gondor and Arnor, and weds Arwen, who has given up elvish immortality for him. Faramir, healed, becomes his Steward and marries Eowyn of Rohan, who turns from war to peace; Merry and Pippin return home grown and renowned. The hobbits find the Shire itself has been seized and ruined by the fallen Saruman and his men, and they lead their people to drive the invaders out; Saruman is killed by his own servant, and the land is cleaned and restored. Sam marries and rebuilds, planting the Shire anew. But Frodo cannot recover from the wounds and the burden he carried. Finding no lasting peace in the home he saved, he leaves it to Sam and sails from the Grey Havens with Bilbo, Gandalf, and the last elves, over the sea and out of Middle-earth. The age of the elves ends, and Sam turns back to his ordinary life, the tale complete.
recaps.in_short: As Sauron's war breaks over the free peoples, the wizard Gandalf and the hobbit Pippin help defend Gondor's capital, Minas Tirith, while the ranger Aragorn takes a hidden road through the Paths of the Dead to raise reinforcements. The city is besieged by the Witch-king's host; Rohan rides to its aid, King Theoden falls, and the lady Eowyn and the hobbit Merry kill the Witch-king. Aragorn arrives with fresh strength and the battle is won, though the Steward Denethor despairs and takes his own life, nearly killing his son Faramir. To draw Sauron's eye from the ring, the captains march their small army to the Black Gate as a decoy. Meanwhile Sam rescues Frodo from an orc-tower, and the two struggle across Mordor to Mount Doom. There Frodo's will fails and he claims the ring, but Gollum seizes it and falls into the fire, destroying it and Sauron's power. Aragorn is crowned king and weds Arwen. The hobbits return home to find the Shire despoiled and set it right, but Frodo, too wounded within to heal, at last sails over the sea, leaving Sam behind.

recaps.text: The One Ring must be destroyed in the fire of Mordor, and the hobbit Frodo Baggins carries it there with his servant Sam. The Fellowship that set out with him has long since broken. The wizard Gandalf, thought lost after falling with a demon of fire in Moria, returned as Gandalf the White. With him, the ranger Aragorn, the elf Legolas, the dwarf Gimli, and the reawakened King Theoden of Rohan defeated the treacherous wizard Saruman and won the battle of Helm's Deep. But the hobbit Pippin looked into an enemy seeing-stone and drew the eye of the Dark Lord Sauron, whose armies are now massing against the realm of Gondor; Gandalf has ridden to its capital, Minas Tirith, to prepare its defence. Far to the east, the creature Gollum led Frodo and Sam toward Mordor by a secret way and then betrayed them to the giant spider Shelob. Frodo was stung and taken prisoner by orcs into the tower of Cirith Ungol. Sam, who briefly bore the ring, has learned his master still lives, and stands alone outside the tower, resolved to rescue him.

Gandalf and Pippin ride to Minas Tirith, the fortress-city of Gondor, where Pippin is presented to Denethor, the ruling Steward, and pledges his service in gratitude for Boromir, Denethor's dead son. The city braces for siege as the shadow of Mordor grows and the beacons are lit calling Rohan to aid. Denethor, proud and grim, mistrusts Gandalf and grieves bitterly for Boromir while slighting his surviving son, Faramir. Meanwhile Aragorn, parting from the main host, takes a desperate road: warned that time is short, he passes with a small grey-cloaked company through the haunted Paths of the Dead beneath the mountains, summoning the spirits of oath-breakers who long ago failed Gondor and are bound to answer his claim as heir to its ancient kings. Legolas, Gimli, and the Rangers of the North go with him into the dark, gambling that this hidden road will let him strike the enemy from an unexpected quarter.

Rohan gathers at Theoden's call; the lady Eowyn, forbidden to ride to war, goes secretly in disguise and takes the young hobbit Merry, also left behind, up before her. Sauron's host, led by the Lord of the Nazgul, the deadly Witch-king, crosses the river, breaks the outer city, and lays siege to Minas Tirith, hurling fire and terror over its walls. Faramir is gravely wounded in the retreat and lies as if dying. Just as the great gate is broken and the Witch-king rides through, the horns of Rohan sound: Theoden's riders charge onto the fields and scatter the besiegers. Theoden is thrown down by the Witch-king's flying steed, but Eowyn stands over him and, with Merry striking from behind, destroys the Nazgul-lord, whom no living man could kill; both are grievously hurt. Theoden dies. At the crisis Aragorn arrives up the river in captured black ships, not the enemy reinforcement the city feared but Gondor's own strength gathered on the way, and the tide of the battle turns to victory.

Despairing and half-mad with grief and the lies the enemy has fed him through a hidden seeing-stone, the Steward Denethor believes all is lost and tries to burn himself and the wounded, still-living Faramir together on a funeral pyre. Pippin runs for help, and Gandalf and the guards arrive in time to save Faramir, but Denethor takes his own life in the flames. In the aftermath, Aragorn comes quietly to the Houses of Healing, where many lie struck down by the deadly Black Breath of the Nazgul. With an ancient healing gift long said to mark the true king, he draws Faramir, Eowyn, and Merry back from the shadow of death and tends many others, though he does not yet claim the crown openly. The battle for the city is won, but at heavy cost, and the survivors know Sauron's full strength has not yet been spent.

With the city saved but weakened, the captains of the west take counsel. Gandalf argues that they cannot win by force against Mordor's numbers; their only hope lies with Frodo, who may still be carrying the ring toward the Mountain of Fire. To buy him time and draw Sauron's attention away from his own land, they resolve on a reckless gamble: to march the small remaining army of Gondor and Rohan straight to the Black Gate of Mordor and challenge the Enemy openly, as though they meant to invade. Aragorn, Gandalf, and the others lead this host east and stand before the gate. A mouthpiece of Sauron comes out and taunts them, displaying gear taken from Frodo as proof the ring-bearer has been caught, but Gandalf refuses the enemy's terms. The gates open and Mordor's vast army pours out to surround the tiny host, and the desperate last battle begins.

Meanwhile Sam storms the tower of Cirith Ungol, where the orc garrison has largely slaughtered itself in a quarrel over Frodo's captured gear, and rescues Frodo from his cell. Disguised in orc-armor, the two make their way down into Mordor and across its bleak, ash-choked plains toward Mount Doom, suffering terribly from thirst, exhaustion, and the ever-growing weight of the ring, which now torments Frodo almost beyond bearing; near the end Sam carries him bodily up the slope. They are stalked the whole way by Gollum. At the very edge of the fire, Frodo's will finally breaks: he refuses to destroy the ring and claims it for himself, slipping it on. Gollum attacks, bites the ring, and Frodo's finger with it, from his hand, and then, gloating over his prize, loses his footing and falls with it into the fire. The ring is unmade. With its destruction Sauron's power collapses utterly: his towers fall, his armies at the Black Gate are broken, and eagles carry Gandalf to pluck Frodo and Sam from the erupting mountain.

Frodo and Sam wake safe, healed, and honored on the field of Cormallen, hailed by the whole surviving army as the ring-bearers who won the war, and reunited joyfully with their friends and with Gandalf. The victors return to Minas Tirith. Aragorn is crowned King Elessar, uniting the long-divided realms of Gondor and Arnor and beginning to set them in order; Faramir is confirmed as Steward and made a prince of a restored province. When the elves come south for the coronation, Aragorn weds Arwen, Elrond's daughter, who has chosen a mortal life to be with him. Eowyn and Faramir, healed together in the Houses of Healing, come to love one another and are betrothed, and Eowyn turns from war to a life of peace and healing. The great alliance holds in friendship, and the surviving members of the Fellowship prepare at last to go their separate ways home.

The companions travel north together and part one by one along the way; Theoden is laid to rest in Rohan, and the hobbits eventually turn for home alone after a parting from Gandalf. Reaching the Shire, they find it has been seized and spoiled in their absence: trees felled, homes torn down, and the people bullied by ruffians under a hidden boss who proves to be the fallen wizard Saruman, taking petty revenge. No longer the timid hobbits who left, Merry and Pippin rouse the Shire-folk, and in a short, sharp rebellion the invaders are driven out and defeated. Saruman is confronted and, when he tries a last cruelty, is killed by his own abused servant Wormtongue at Frodo's very door; Frodo, sickened of killing, had tried to spare even him. The hobbits set about clearing the wreckage and healing the land, and Sam uses a gift of earth and a seed from Galadriel to help it bloom again swiftly.

The Shire recovers and even flourishes; Sam marries Rosie and starts a family, and Merry and Pippin are honored as heroes of the wider world. But Frodo does not fully heal. The wound from the cursed blade at Weathertop, the sting of Shelob, and above all the long burden of the ring have hurt him in body and spirit past mending, and he finds he can no longer feel at home in the land he saved. Quietly, he sets his affairs in order and passes his book and his home to Sam. At the Grey Havens he joins Bilbo, Gandalf, and the last of the elves leaving Middle-earth, and takes ship over the sea to a place of rest and healing beyond the world. Sam, Merry, and Pippin watch the ship go from the shore. Sam then returns home to his wife and daughter, and the long tale closes on him coming back to a full house and an ordinary life, the world saved and the age of the elves and their magic passing away.

characters.description: The fourth of the nine, holding together a group that has just lost one of its members and been betrayed by another. He has stopped treating the war as something to survive and started treating it as something to win, which makes him harder on the people around him and on himself. His Legacies are now broad enough that he is the group's most flexible fighter, and his priorities are recovering Ella and finding out what the Mogadorians are actually building on Earth.
characters.name: John Smith

characters.description: The youngest Garde, one of the book's narrators, and a prisoner aboard Setrakus Ra's warship. She is not being tortured or killed, which frightens her more than either would: she is being talked to, taught, and shown things, and she is expected to agree with them. Her Legacies reach minds and dreams, and they are the only way she has of doing anything at all from inside a Mogadorian ship.
characters.name: Ella

characters.description: A young Mogadorian, son of a senior officer, and one of the book's narrators. As a boy he was used in an experiment that connected his mind to that of a dead Garde, and he has carried her memories and her point of view ever since, along with an earth-shaking Legacy no Mogadorian should have. That inheritance turned him against everything he was raised in. He has spent years surviving alone between the two sides, and he knows the Mogadorian order, its installations, and its plans from the inside.
characters.name: Adam

characters.description: The first of the nine, killed years before the Garde ever met each other. She survives in this book as the presence in Adam's mind, the source of his memories of Lorien and of the conscience that made him break with his own people. Through him she is the closest thing to a witness the Garde have to their own earliest losses.
characters.name: Number One

characters.description: The seventh of the nine, and a different person since the Everglades. Grief has given her a Legacy of lethal cold and taken away most of her patience; she is now among the most dangerous of the Garde rather than its healer. She wants Number Five, and everyone around her knows it.
characters.name: Marina

characters.description: The sixth of the nine, invisible when she chooses and able to call down weather. She is the group's best soldier and its most willing to operate independently, and she takes on the missions that require going somewhere dangerous with almost no support.
characters.name: Number Six

characters.description: The ninth of the nine, whose Chicago base and resources have kept the group operating. Fast, strong, and able to move along any surface, he is more use than ever now that the war has turned into raids on fortified positions, and no more inclined to caution than he ever was.
characters.name: Number Nine

characters.description: The fifth of the nine, who killed Number Eight and went over to the Mogadorians, and who lost an eye to Marina doing it. He can fly and can take on the properties of whatever he touches. He is now on the enemy's side of the war, with the Garde's own knowledge of how they operate.
characters.name: Number Five

characters.description: John's human friend, who has been in this war since Ohio without a single Legacy to show for it. He handles the group's technology and research alongside his father and refuses to be left behind on any operation, which is a standing argument he mostly wins.
characters.name: Sam Goode

characters.description: Sam's father, whose recovered memories of meeting the Loric ships in 1980 and hiding the children who arrived on them are now the group's best source of intelligence about what the Loric left on Earth. He works the research side of the war rather than the fighting side.
characters.name: Malcolm Goode

characters.description: John's girlfriend from Paradise, fully part of the group's operations now. She has no powers, trains and fights anyway, and is one of the few people John will still take advice from.
characters.name: Sarah Hart

characters.description: The Mogadorian leader. He has Ella aboard his ship and is spending time on her personally rather than disposing of her, and what he wants from the Garde has changed: he is preparing to be seen by the human world rather than to keep operating out of caves and disguised compounds.
characters.name: Setrakus Ra

characters.description: The Chimaera who has guarded John since Lorien, able to take any animal's shape. He is no longer the only one of his kind the Garde know about.
characters.name: Bernie Kosar

recaps.ending: Setrakus Ra's plan turns out to be public rather than covert. Having spent years operating out of hidden bases, he presents himself openly to the world's governments as a visitor offering help, in a form humans will accept, and much of the world is prepared to listen. Then the Mogadorian warships decloak over New York and other cities and the invasion begins in the open. The Garde are split when it starts: Six, Marina, and Adam are in Mexico looking for the Loric sanctuary Malcolm Goode remembered, while John, Sam, Sarah, Nine, and Malcolm are in New York, where the first ships arrive. Ella is still aboard Setrakus Ra's ship, now knowing exactly what he wants from her and refusing it. Adam has burned his own side for good and is trusted, if not liked, by the Garde. The war stops being a secret hunt for nine children and becomes an open invasion of Earth, with the Garde outnumbered, scattered across two continents, and holding one advantage: they know what the Loric left behind here, and the Mogadorians have not found it yet.
recaps.in_short: After Number Eight's death and Ella's capture, the Garde regroup around three things: recovering Ella, understanding what the Mogadorians are building, and Marina's determination to find Number Five. Ella, held aboard Setrakus Ra's warship, learns that he is her grandfather and that he intends her to inherit what he has built, and she resists while trying to warn the others in their sleep. Adam, a Mogadorian who carries the memories of Number One after an experiment on him as a boy, and the earth-shaking Legacy that came with them, defects and brings the Garde what he knows. Together they raid Ashwood Estates, a Mogadorian settlement in Virginia disguised as an ordinary suburb, and find beneath it the enemy's technology, captive Chimaerae, and evidence of a plan to approach the world's governments openly. The group splits: Six, Marina, and Adam go to Mexico to find a Loric sanctuary, and John's group goes to New York. Setrakus Ra presents himself to humanity as a benefactor, and then the warships decloak and the invasion begins.

recaps.text: Nine Loric children were sent to Earth with guardians called Cepans when the Mogadorians destroyed Lorien. Numbers One, Two, and Three were killed first. Number Four, John Smith, was found in Ohio, where his guardian Henri died; Number Six joined him, along with his human friend Sam Goode and a Chimaera called Bernie Kosar. Number Seven, called Marina, was found in Spain; the orphan she protected was Number Ten, called Ella, from a second Loric ship. Number Nine was freed from a Mogadorian mountain base, and Number Eight was found in India. All of their Cepans are now dead, including Ella's, and the charm that once made the nine killable only in order no longer protects them. Sam's father Malcolm was recovered from Mogadorian hands, and his returning memories revealed that humans met the Loric ships when they landed. Number Five was found last, and betrayed them: he had already made terms with the Mogadorians, and he killed Number Eight. Marina, in grief, developed a Legacy of lethal cold and took one of Five's eyes. Setrakus Ra took Ella captive. Five of the nine remain, and one of them is on the enemy's side.

The Garde pull themselves back together after Florida. John takes the group's losses as a reason to fight harder rather than to hide, Marina has come out of it colder and more dangerous, and everyone's first objective is Ella. Ella, meanwhile, is aboard Setrakus Ra's warship, held in reasonable comfort and treated as a guest rather than a prisoner, which unsettles her more than a cell would. He talks to her, shows her things, and appears to be waiting for her to come round to something. A third strand opens with Adam, a young Mogadorian and the son of a senior officer, who was used as a boy in an experiment that joined his mind to a dead Garde's. He has carried her memories ever since, along with a Legacy no Mogadorian should possess, and he has been living between the two sides.

Adam breaks with his own people for good and makes contact with the Garde, offering what he knows about Mogadorian installations, chains of command, and intentions. He is a Mogadorian asking Loric survivors to trust him weeks after one of their own betrayed them, and the reception is what would be expected. Number Five is now openly on the enemy's side, and Marina intends to find him. Aboard the warship, Setrakus Ra's interest in Ella becomes explicit: he has a specific role in mind for her, and he expects her to accept it. Her Legacies work on minds, so the only thing she can do from inside is reach for the Garde in their sleep and try to tell them what she has learned.

Setrakus Ra tells Ella what she is to him: she is his granddaughter, and he means her to inherit what he has built rather than to die with the rest of the Garde. He offers her a version of the war in which she is on the winning side and her people survive, and he makes it as reasonable as he can. Ella refuses and keeps refusing, while continuing to gather everything she can about his plans. On Earth, Adam's intelligence gives the Garde a target that changes their understanding of the enemy entirely: Ashwood Estates, a Mogadorian settlement in Virginia that looks from the road like an ordinary American suburb, complete with houses and lawns, and which has been operating for years within reach of the American capital.

The Garde raid Ashwood Estates with Adam guiding them. Beneath the suburb they find the real installation: Mogadorian technology, records, and Chimaerae held in stasis, Loric creatures like Bernie Kosar that the enemy captured rather than killed. They also find evidence of what Setrakus Ra is actually preparing, and it is not another hunting operation. The Mogadorians intend to approach the governments of Earth openly, presenting themselves as visitors offering help. The raid destroys the site and confirms Adam as an ally, at the cost of announcing to the Mogadorian leadership that the Garde have someone on the inside.

With the Mogadorian plan exposed, the Garde have two problems that cannot be solved in one place, and they split. Six, Marina, and Adam head for Mexico, following what Malcolm Goode remembered about a Loric sanctuary hidden there, on the reasoning that whatever the Loric left on Earth is the only thing that might change the odds. John, Sam, Sarah, Nine, and Malcolm head for New York, where Setrakus Ra intends to make his public approach to the world's governments. Ella, still aboard his ship, now understands the full shape of what he is planning and can do nothing about it except refuse him. Both groups are moving toward events they cannot stop, and the Garde have never been more thinly spread.

Setrakus Ra presents himself to humanity, in a form humans will accept, as a visitor offering aid rather than a conqueror, and enough of the world is willing to hear him out. The deception holds only briefly: the Mogadorian warships decloak over New York and other cities and the invasion begins openly. John's group is in New York when the first ships arrive; Six, Marina, and Adam are in Mexico, still searching for the sanctuary; Ella is aboard Setrakus Ra's ship, refusing the inheritance he has offered her. Adam has destroyed any way back to his own people. The war has changed shape entirely: it is no longer a hidden hunt for a handful of children, but an open invasion of Earth, with the Garde outnumbered, separated across two continents, and holding only one real advantage, which is that they know the Loric left something behind here and the Mogadorians have not found it.

characters.description: The fourth of the nine, now travelling with Number Nine after freeing him from the Mogadorian base in West Virginia. He has lost his guardian Henri, been separated from Six, and left Sam Goode in enemy hands, and getting Sam back is the thing he will not be argued out of. His Legacies are strengthening but his judgement is still driven by the people he refuses to abandon, which Nine treats as a weakness and Six treats as a liability.
characters.name: John Smith

characters.description: The ninth of the nine, recently freed after a long imprisonment and impatient to hit back. He is the strongest of the Garde met so far, fast, and able to run along walls and ceilings as though gravity does not apply to him. He was raised in Chicago by a Cepan who trained him in a purpose-built penthouse, and he returns there with John. Confident to the point of recklessness, he treats caution as cowardice and wants to attack the Mogadorians directly rather than keep hiding.
characters.name: Number Nine

characters.description: The sixth of the nine, and the most capable fighter among them. Having pulled Marina and Ella out of Spain, she now leads their half of the group, planning routes, forging papers, and deciding what risks are worth taking. She can turn invisible and call down storms, and she is the one pushing hardest to gather every surviving Garde before the Mogadorians can isolate them again.
characters.name: Number Six

characters.description: The seventh of the nine, out of the Spanish convent where she spent most of her life and grieving the guardian and the friend who died getting her out. Her Legacies are healing, breathing underwater, and seeing in the dark, and she is only now learning to fight. She travels with Six, Ella, and Crayton, out of her depth but determined not to be the one who has to be protected.
characters.name: Marina

characters.description: The tenth Garde, a child who came to Earth on a second Loric ship that arrived after the first, raised by her Cepan Crayton. She spent years hidden as an orphan in a Spanish convent and is now travelling openly with the others. Her Legacies are still emerging and unusual: she can shift her apparent age and reach other minds, including in sleep. She is the youngest of the group and the one everyone else tries to keep out of the fighting.
characters.name: Ella

characters.description: Ella's Cepan, who came on the second Loric ship and carries the history of Lorien's fall that the nine were never told, including how the second ship came to be launched at all. Calm and methodical, he takes charge of moving Six, Marina, and Ella across the world and follows the reports that lead them toward India.
characters.name: Crayton

characters.description: The eighth of the nine, found in the mountains of India, where villagers have spent years telling stories about a boy in a cave who can do impossible things and have come to treat him as a god. He can teleport himself and others and can change his shape at will, which makes him the hardest of the Garde to pin down and, at first meeting, the hardest to trust. He has been alone for a long time and has been guarding something in the mountain that concerns all of them.
characters.name: Number Eight

characters.description: John's human friend from Paradise, captured by the Mogadorians during the escape from their West Virginia base and held since. He has no Legacies and no protection, and the fact that he was taken because he insisted on helping is what drives John's plans through most of the book.
characters.name: Sam Goode

characters.description: Number Nine's Cepan, who raised and trained him in Chicago and built the fortified penthouse and training hall the two of them used. He did not survive the attack in which Nine was captured. He is present in the book only through Nine's memories and through the equipment, resources, and defences he left behind.
characters.name: Sandor

characters.description: The Chimaera who has guarded John since Lorien, usually in the shape of a beagle. He travels with John and Nine, changes into whatever the fight requires, and can communicate with John directly.
characters.name: Bernie Kosar

characters.description: The girl John left in Paradise, Ohio. He has not been able to establish whether she had anything to do with the agents who were waiting for him there, and the question sits between him and any attempt to contact her.
characters.name: Sarah Hart

characters.description: The leader of the Mogadorians, the figure behind the destruction of Lorien and the hunt for the nine. Until now he has been a name in Loric history and an authority the soldiers invoke rather than anyone the Garde have seen. What the Garde learn about him in this book is that he is on Earth, that he is directing the search personally, and that he is far beyond an ordinary Mogadorian officer.
characters.name: Setrakus Ra

recaps.ending: The two halves of the group converge on the Mogadorian installation in New Mexico. John and Nine break in to free Sam Goode, and Six, Marina, Ella, and Eight reach them, so that for the first time since Lorien the surviving Garde stand together in one place: Four, Six, Seven, Eight, Nine, and Ten, with Sam and Bernie Kosar. Setrakus Ra confronts them in person and proves to be something far worse than the soldiers they have been fighting, but united they are able to hold him and force him to withdraw rather than being picked off individually, which is the first thing that has ever worked. Sam is freed. The victory is partial and expensive: Crayton, Ella's guardian, was killed in the mountains of India, and the Garde have now lost every adult who came with them from Lorien except the knowledge those adults passed on. The survivors leave together for Chicago and Nine's fortified penthouse, which becomes their base. The charm that protected them by number is gone, so from this point any of them can be killed at any time, and the only defence they have is the one that just worked: staying together.
recaps.in_short: The surviving Garde spend the book converging. John and Number Nine hole up in Nine's fortified Chicago penthouse, argue about tactics, and then set out for a Mogadorian installation in New Mexico to free Sam Goode, hunted the whole way by federal agents. Six, Marina, Ella, and Ella's guardian Crayton follow reports of a boy in the Himalayas who performs miracles and find Number Eight, who can teleport and change shape and who has been guarding a cave whose paintings appear to show the Garde's own future. The Mogadorians attack them in the mountains: Crayton is killed and Six is taken prisoner. Marina, Ella, and Eight escape and go after her. All of the survivors meet at the New Mexico base, where they free Sam and face Setrakus Ra, the Mogadorian leader, in person for the first time. Fighting together they force him to withdraw. The Garde leave for Chicago as a single group of six, having lost the last of their Cepans and the protection of the charm that once made them killable only in order.

recaps.text: Nine Loric children were sent to Earth with adult guardians called Cepans when the Mogadorians destroyed Lorien, protected by a charm that let them be killed only in the order of their numbers. Numbers One, Two, and Three are dead. Number Four grew up as John Smith, settled in Paradise, Ohio, and was found there; the battle that followed killed his guardian Henri but brought him Number Six, the most experienced of the survivors, and revealed that his dog Bernie Kosar is a Chimaera, a Loric shape-shifter. John left Ohio with Six and his human friend Sam Goode, and Sarah Hart behind. In Spain, Number Seven, called Marina, had spent years in a convent orphanage with a Cepan who had abandoned the mission; when the Mogadorians attacked Santa Teresa, that guardian and a local friend were killed, Six arrived, and the orphan girl Ella turned out to be Number Ten, from a second Loric ship, collected by her Cepan Crayton. John and Sam meanwhile broke into a Mogadorian mountain base in West Virginia and freed Number Nine, but Sam was captured. Six survivors are alive in two groups, each looking for the other, and the Mogadorians hold Sam.

John and Nine, with Bernie Kosar, go to ground in Chicago in the penthouse Nine's Cepan Sandor built and equipped: fortified, stocked, and fitted with a training hall. Sandor died when Nine was captured, and Nine has come back to an empty version of his old life. The two of them train and clash constantly. Nine wants to take the war to the Mogadorians immediately; John wants to find Sam Goode, who was captured covering their escape from West Virginia, and refuses to move on to anything else first. Meanwhile Six, Marina, Ella, and Ella's Cepan Crayton are out of Spain and moving. Crayton begins filling in what the nine were never told about Lorien's last days and the second ship that carried Ella. Six is running their half of the group, and the news reports Crayton is tracking point them toward the mountains of India.

John and Nine leave Chicago for the American southwest, following what they can piece together about where Sam is being held. The manhunt for John is now a national one, and federal agents are as much of a problem as Mogadorians. The tension between the two Garde is constant: Nine is faster, stronger, and openly contemptuous of John's attachments, while John will not be talked out of the rescue. In India, Six's group reaches the foothills and starts asking about the stories that brought them there: villagers speak of a boy who has lived in a mountain cave for years and who can do things nobody can explain, and who is treated locally as a god. Crayton believes the stories describe one of the nine.

In the mountains Six, Marina, Ella, and Crayton find Number Eight. He can teleport himself and other people and can change his shape at will, and his first instinct on being found is to test the strangers rather than trust them, which makes the meeting an ugly one. Once he accepts who they are, he shows them what he has been living beside: a cave whose walls carry paintings that seem to record events the Garde have not lived through yet, including images of the survivors themselves. The find suggests the Loric left more behind on Earth than nine children and their Chests, and that someone expected them to come here. John and Nine, still travelling, close on the site in New Mexico where they believe Sam is held.

The Mogadorians attack in the Himalayas, in strength and with the clear intention of taking the Garde alive rather than killing them. The fight in the mountains costs the group badly: Crayton is killed, and with him goes the last adult who remembered Lorien first-hand. Number Six is captured and carried off. Marina, Ella, and Eight escape and immediately set out to get her back, with Eight's teleporting the only reason they can move fast enough to try. Marina, who spent years being told she would never need to fight, is now doing nothing else. In America, John and Nine reach the Mogadorian installation in New Mexico and begin working out how to get inside.

John and Nine get into the New Mexico base, a large underground Mogadorian facility, and fight their way toward the cells. Marina, Ella, and Eight are converging on the same place, and Six, held prisoner there, is being kept alive deliberately. What the Garde find inside makes the scale of the Mogadorian presence on Earth undeniable: this is not a hunting party but an established operation with laboratories, garrisons, and prisoners. Sam Goode is found alive. As the fighting spreads through the base, the separate groups of Garde reach each other, and it becomes clear that the Mogadorian leadership has arranged the confrontation as much as they have.

All of the surviving Garde stand together for the first time: John, Six, Marina, Eight, Nine, and Ella, with Sam freed and Bernie Kosar with them. Setrakus Ra, the Mogadorian leader, faces them in person, and he is far beyond the soldiers they have fought so far. Individually none of them can stand against him; together they hold him long enough to force him to break off, which is the first real evidence that Six's argument was right and that gathering was worth what it cost. They get out and leave for Chicago and Nine's penthouse, which becomes their base of operations. The cost of the book is heavy: Crayton is dead, the last of their Cepans, and the charm that once made the nine killable only in order no longer protects anyone. From here every one of them is vulnerable at any moment, and staying together is the only defence they have found.

characters.description: The Nahid healer at the centre of the trilogy: born to Banu Manizheh and a human father, raised as an orphan thief and con artist in Ottoman Cairo, and brought to the djinn city of Daevabad to take up a name, a family and a set of obligations she never asked for.
characters.name: Nahri

characters.description: The devout younger prince of Daevabad, raised at the Citadel to command his brother's armies and drawn instead to the cause of the city's part-human shafit. Marid magic left in him after the events of the first novel permanently changes what he is.
characters.name: Alizayd

characters.description: The Nahids' warrior, called the Scourge of Qui-zi by the tribes he fought during the war that ended Nahid rule. Enslaved by the ifrit for centuries, killed on Daevabad's lake and raised again by Banu Manizheh, he spends the trilogy carrying out orders he becomes steadily less able to justify.
characters.name: Dara

characters.description: The most gifted Nahid healer of her generation, believed murdered by ifrit for twenty years and in fact alive, working toward the recovery of the city her family lost. Nahri's mother and Jamshid's, and the trilogy's central antagonist.
characters.name: Manizheh

characters.description: Ghassan's elder son and emir of Daevabad, a diplomat and a drinker who is far fonder of company, poetry and wine than of power, and who loves Jamshid e-Pramukh.
characters.name: Muntadhir

characters.description: Kaveh e-Pramukh's son, an archer and Muntadhir's closest companion, and, unknown to him for most of the trilogy, Banu Manizheh's son and Nahri's half-brother.
characters.name: Jamshid

characters.description: Ali's mother, an Ayaanle noblewoman of Ta Ntry and Ghassan's queen, whose money, family connections and willingness to scheme repeatedly change what her son is able to do.
characters.name: Hatset

characters.description: Ghassan's daughter and Ali's older sister, the most politically adept of the Qahtani children, who works from inside the court in ways neither of her brothers can.
characters.name: Zaynab

characters.description: King of Daevabad through the first two novels, bearer of Suleiman's seal, and the head of the family that took the city from the Nahids fourteen centuries earlier. He holds six mutually hostile tribes together by knowing exactly what each person under him has to lose.
characters.name: Ghassan

recaps.ending: The collection has no single plot to resolve. It closes with two pieces that sit at or after the trilogy's last page: an alternative epilogue to The Empire of Gold, presenting a version of the ending that the published novels did not use, and a short final piece from Nahri's perspective. Because so many of the entries depend on knowing how the trilogy turns out, the collection as a whole is a full-spoiler companion to the three novels rather than a way into them.
recaps.in_short: The River of Silver is a companion collection to the Daevabad trilogy: a set of short pieces, outtakes and deleted scenes told from the viewpoints of characters the novels mostly kept at a distance, among them Manizheh, Duriya, Hatset, Muntadhir, Jamshid, Zaynab, Dara, Ali and Nahri. The pieces are not arranged as a continuous story and are not confined to one point in the timeline: they range from long before The City of Brass to after the close of The Empire of Gold, and several of them depend on knowing how the trilogy ends. The book finishes with an alternative epilogue to The Empire of Gold, a version of the ending that was not the one published, followed by a short closing piece from Nahri. It is written to be read after the three novels, not alongside them.

recaps.text: A note before starting: The River of Silver is a companion collection rather than a fourth novel, and its pieces are scattered across the whole timeline, from decades before The City of Brass to after the final page of The Empire of Gold. It assumes you have finished all three books, and it will spoil them. Previously, in the Daevabad trilogy: Nahri, a con artist in Ottoman Cairo, discovered she carried the blood of the Nahids, the healer family that once ruled the hidden djinn city of Daevabad, and was brought there by Darayavahoush the Afshin. She was installed in the palace of King Ghassan al Qahtani, whose ancestors took the city from hers, married to his heir Muntadhir, and befriended his younger son Alizayd. Dara was killed on the city's lake and raised again by Banu Manizheh, the Nahid healer everyone believed dead, who is Nahri's mother and also, it emerges, the mother of Jamshid e-Pramukh. Manizheh seized Daevabad during the Navasatem festival, killing Ghassan and most of the city's Geziri, and the city lost its magic when Alizayd fled with Suleiman's seal. Nahri and Ali returned from exile with allies and a marid bargain; Manizheh was defeated and killed, Ali was gravely changed by the magic that saved him, and Nahri ended the seal's absolute power rather than claim it, restoring Daevabad's magic and leaving the city to a shared government that includes the shafit for the first time.

The first run of pieces is told from the viewpoints of Manizheh, Duriya, Hatset, Muntadhir, Jamshid and Dara. They sit outside the novels' main narrative, filling in the lives, histories and private calculations of characters the trilogy largely showed from the outside or from an unfriendly angle. They are not in chronological order relative to one another, and several are set well before the events of The City of Brass.

The middle of the collection continues with further pieces from Jamshid, Ali, an observer identified only as the Scout, Nahri, Ali again, Zaynab and Muntadhir. Like the earlier entries they move back and forth across the trilogy's span rather than advancing a single storyline, and they increasingly assume knowledge of events from the later novels.

The collection closes with an alternative epilogue to The Empire of Gold, an account of how the trilogy's final scene might have gone in a version that was not published, and then a last short piece from Nahri's perspective. Both belong after the trilogy's conclusion and both take its outcome as read.

characters.description: A royal Moroi spirit user, newly married and living at the Moroi Court, where his wife is safe only so long as she does not step outside its boundaries. He is back on his medication and clean, which steadies him and takes away his magic, and every decision in front of him is about whether to give that up again. One of the book's two narrators.
characters.name: Adrian Ivashkov

characters.description: A former Alchemist, a trained witch, and a fugitive from the order that raised her. She is married to a Moroi and sheltering at the Moroi Court, protected by the queen's goodwill and confined by it, since the Alchemists are waiting the moment she leaves. Months of re-education have left marks she is not discussing. The book's other narrator.
characters.name: Sydney Sage

characters.description: The Moroi queen's younger half-sister, whose existence is the only thing that lets her sister keep the throne, and who has spent years being moved, hidden and guarded because of it. She is bonded to Adrian and has grown up considerably since the hiding began. She goes missing early in this book.
characters.name: Jill Dragomir

characters.description: The dhampir who has guarded Jill since the beginning of the hiding, and who takes her disappearance as his own failure. Competent, self-punishing and unwilling to be left out of the search.
characters.name: Eddie Castile

characters.description: The Moroi queen, and the reason Jill has spent years in hiding: without a second living Dragomir her claim to the throne fails. She shelters Sydney and Adrian at Court against considerable political cost.
characters.name: Vasilisa Dragomir

characters.description: A Moroi spirit user and restored former Strigoi, one of the few people who can approach the group's problems from the magical side rather than the political one.
characters.name: Sonya Karp

characters.description: A dhampir guardian of formidable reputation, once Strigoi and restored, now serving at Court and unhappy with how little the search for a missing girl is officially permitted to do.
characters.name: Dimitri Belikov

characters.description: The queen's guardian, blunt and impatient with protocol, and one of the few people at Court who treats Sydney as an ally rather than a liability.
characters.name: Rose Hathaway

characters.description: The young dhampir guardian who was part of the Palm Springs detail, and the father of Olive Sinclair's child - a fact that has upended everything he believed about duty and about himself.
characters.name: Neil Raymond

characters.description: The witch who trained Sydney, still the source of the workings that can do what neither Moroi magic nor guardian legwork can.
characters.name: Jaclyn Terwilliger

characters.description: The small scaled creature Sydney and Adrian summoned together, which spends most of its life dormant as a charm and wakes up hungry. It is bonded to both of them and turns out to be more useful than either expected.
characters.name: Hopper

characters.description: A Moroi who was Strigoi and was restored by her sister's spirit magic, pregnant by a dhampir with a child that should not be possible. She is in hiding from everyone who would want to study her, her child, or both.
characters.name: Olive Sinclair

characters.description: The dhampir raised among the Keepers, the community that lives outside Moroi law in the Appalachian backcountry. Her family and her people's customs matter a great deal to where this search leads.
characters.name: Angeline Dawes

characters.description: Sydney's younger sister, an Alchemist who reported her and has since watched the consequences. She is the group's only line into the order, and trusting her is a decision with no safe version.
characters.name: Zoe Sage

characters.description: Sydney's former lab partner and a former Warrior of Light, still outside both of the societies that shaped him and still willing to help the people who cost him them.
characters.name: Trey Juarez

characters.description: Sydney's father, a career Alchemist who regards his daughter's marriage as proof of everything he warned about, and who is not a neutral party in what the order does next.
characters.name: Jared Sage

recaps.ending: Jill is found alive and brought back, and the abduction that removed her is undone. Because the whole danger to her rested on a single rule - that a royal line needs more than one living member for its claim to stand - the resolution is to remove the rule rather than to hide her better: with the law changed, killing Jill no longer unseats a queen, and the years of hiding end. Jill comes back to her own life, and she and Eddie, who has guarded her since the beginning and refused to want anything for himself, are finally together. Olive Sinclair does not survive: her son is born, the first child known to be conceived between a restored Moroi and a dhampir, and he is hidden away to be raised out of reach of Moroi politics and of the Alchemists, both of whom would treat him as evidence rather than a child. Neil is left with a son he cannot openly claim. Sydney's confrontation with her own order and her own family closes the pursuit that has followed her since her escape, and she and Adrian are able to stop running: they stay at Court, married and no longer in hiding, with Sydney free to study and Adrian steady for the first time in his life. The Palm Springs household scatters into lives its members chose.
recaps.in_short: Sydney and Adrian are married and sheltering at the Moroi Court, safe only inside its boundaries while the Alchemists wait outside for Sydney to leave. Then Jill vanishes. Adrian's bond tells him she is alive but not where, and the official search is limited by exactly the politics that put her in danger. Sydney and Adrian leave the safety of Court to look for her themselves, following the trail through the Moroi world, the Alchemists and the Keepers, the community living outside Moroi law where Olive Sinclair has gone to hide the pregnancy that should be impossible. Sydney's magic, her teacher, and the small creature she and Adrian summoned all matter more than any of the official machinery. Olive's son is born and Olive does not survive; the child is hidden away from everyone who would treat him as proof of something. Jill is found and recovered, and the law that made her life the guarantee of her sister's throne is changed, ending the hiding for good. Jill and Eddie are together at last, Sydney's pursuit by her order is finally settled, and she and Adrian can live openly.

recaps.text: Previously: Sydney Sage, an Alchemist, spent two years hiding Jill Dragomir - the Moroi queen's half-sister, whose existence is the only thing keeping her sister on the throne - at a human school in Palm Springs, guarded by the dhampirs Eddie Castile and Angeline Dawes and shadowed by the royal Moroi Adrian Ivashkov, who is psychically bonded to Jill. In that time Sydney discovered she is a witch, was trained in secret by her teacher Jaclyn Terwilliger, learned that the Alchemists' golden lily tattoo carries compulsion, and had hers broken so she could pass as loyal while working against the order. She and Adrian fell in love; her younger sister Zoe found out and reported her, and Sydney was seized and held for months in an Alchemist re-education facility, where she faked conversion to survive. There she found Olive Sinclair, a Moroi restored from Strigoi, pregnant by the dhampir guardian Neil Raymond with a child Moroi biology says cannot exist. Sydney broke both of them out as a rescue party reached the facility, and she and Adrian married in Las Vegas immediately afterwards. Sydney is now a fugitive from her own order, and the only place the Alchemists cannot reach her is the Moroi Court.

Sydney and Adrian are living at the Moroi Court as a married couple, protected by the queen and effectively confined: the Alchemists cannot touch Sydney inside its wards, and are waiting for her to step outside them. It is safety without a life in it - Sydney cannot study, work or go anywhere, and Adrian, back on the medication that steadies his moods at the cost of his magic, has nothing to do but be married. Then Jill disappears. Adrian can tell through the bond that she is alive, and nothing else useful; the guardians' official search is hemmed in by the same politics that made Jill a target in the first place, and the longer she is missing the more precarious the queen's position becomes.

Sydney and Adrian decide that waiting inside the wards is not a plan, and start working the problem themselves. Sydney's magic and Ms. Terwilliger's knowledge give them approaches the Moroi authorities do not have, and the creature they summoned together turns out to have uses nobody anticipated. The search has a second strand: Olive Sinclair, carrying Neil's child, has gone into hiding, because a pregnancy between a restored Moroi and a dhampir is the kind of fact the Alchemists would lock underground and Moroi society would fight over. Neil is not managing either the secrecy or the fatherhood well. The obvious place for someone to disappear into is the Keepers, the community that lives outside Moroi law in the Appalachian backcountry, where Angeline was raised.

The search takes Sydney and Adrian out of Court and into the Keepers' territory, where the group's usual assumptions about law, marriage and status do not apply and where their standing depends on customs Angeline has to translate for them. They find what they came for and rather more besides. Jill's trail, meanwhile, does not lead anywhere simple: it runs through the Moroi world and through the Alchemists at once, and the more they learn about who benefits from her disappearance the clearer it is that this was arranged rather than opportunistic. Sydney's own family becomes part of the problem, and Zoe - who reported her sister and has been living with the result - is the group's only line into the order.

The two strands converge. Olive's pregnancy is far along and cannot be hidden much longer, and the people who want to study her are closing in from more than one direction, while the search for Jill turns from guesswork into a target. Sydney works magic at a scale she has not attempted before, with Ms. Terwilliger's help and at real cost, because ordinary investigation has run out of road. Adrian faces the choice the whole book has been driving at: his medication keeps him functional and takes away the spirit magic that could actually find Jill, and there is only one way to have both problems solved at once. Sydney's confrontation with the Alchemists - and with her own father - stops being avoidable.

Olive's child is born. He is a dhampir, the first known to be conceived between a restored Moroi and a dhampir, and his existence changes what the Moroi believe about themselves and what the Alchemists believe about restored Strigoi. Olive does not survive, and the group is left with a newborn who would be treated as evidence by everyone with an interest in him, and who has to be placed somewhere neither side can reach. Neil has a son he cannot claim. At the same time the search for Jill produces the answer: where she is being held, and who arranged it, and why removing her was worth the risk to the people who did it. Sydney and Adrian go after her without waiting for permission from the Court.

Jill is recovered alive. The problem underneath the whole series is then solved at its root rather than patched again: the law that requires a royal line to have more than one living member is changed, so Jill's death would no longer cost her sister the throne, and there is no longer any reason to hide her. Jill goes back to her own life and to Eddie, who has guarded her from the start and finally stops treating what he wants as a professional failing. Sydney's long conflict with the Alchemists and with her family is settled well enough that she is no longer hunted, and she and Adrian stay at Court, married, sober and steady, with Sydney free to study and Adrian with something to do that he chose. Olive's son is hidden away with people who can raise him unremarked, out of reach of Moroi politics and the Alchemists alike, and Neil has to live with that. The Palm Springs household, thrown together by a hiding assignment, scatters into ordinary lives.

characters.description: The self-styled Lord of Rain and Night, once a baron of the kingdom of Araluen. Fifteen years before the story opens he rebelled against King Duncan, was beaten in battle, and withdrew into the bleak Mountains of Rain and Night with the surviving Wargals, brutish beast-soldiers he commands directly with his mind. He has spent the years since brooding on revenge and is patient, calculating, and physically imposing.
characters.name: Morgarath

characters.description: A pair of enormous, near-unkillable creatures Morgarath keeps and sends out as assassins. Shaggy and ape-like, they move faster than their bulk suggests, ordinary arrows barely mark their thick hide, and their red stare freezes a victim in place with terror. They are treated in Araluen as half legend, and almost nobody living has faced one.
characters.name: The Kalkara

characters.description: A slight, quick fifteen-year-old orphan raised as a ward of Castle Redmont, one of five parentless children brought up at the Baron's expense. He knows almost nothing about his parents beyond a claim that his father died as a soldier, and he has always assumed that Battleschool and knighthood are the only way to prove himself worthy of that. He is agile, endlessly curious, a practised climber, and quietly resourceful, none of which looks like the makings of a knight.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: The King's Ranger for Redmont Fief: a short, grim, grey-bearded man in a mottled cloak who appears and disappears without anyone noticing. Ordinary people believe Rangers work sorcery and give him a wide berth. He speaks bluntly and rarely, carries a heavy longbow, a saxe knife and a throwing knife, and has the confidence of the Baron and the King.
characters.name: Halt

characters.description: Lord of Redmont Fief and the man responsible for the castle's wards. He is fair-minded, shrewd about the people who serve him, and fond of a joke that his staff rarely find as funny as he does. He presides over the Choosing, at which each ward is offered, or refused, a craft apprenticeship.
characters.name: Baron Arald

characters.description: A ward of Will's age, big, heavily built, and set on Battleschool from the beginning. He has spent years bullying Will and the smaller wards, and the two of them cordially detest one another as the story opens.
characters.name: Horace Altman

characters.description: A ward of Castle Redmont, tall, fair and unusually self-possessed, with hopes of a place in the fief's Diplomatic Service. She is a steady friend to Will and rather better than he is at keeping her nerve.
characters.name: Alyss Mainwaring

characters.description: A cheerful, round-faced ward with an obvious gift for cooking, who hopes to be taken on by the castle's kitchen master. She is the warmest of the five wards and the least troubled about her future.
characters.name: Jenny Dalby

characters.description: A thin, talkative ward who enjoys an argument for its own sake and is drawn to the scribes and the law. He is the least physical of the five and entirely untroubled by that.
characters.name: George Carter

characters.description: Redmont's Battlemaster, who runs the fief's Battleschool and decides which boys are taken into it. Large, blond and genial, he judges candidates on build and stamina as much as on willingness, and he is on close terms with the Baron and with Halt.
characters.name: Sir Rodney

characters.description: The head of Redmont's Diplomatic Service, a tall, elegant woman who trains couriers and negotiators. She is composed to the point of coolness, misses nothing, and has known Halt for a long time.
characters.name: Lady Pauline

characters.description: The horse assigned to Will: small, barrel-chested and unimpressively shaggy next to a battlehorse, and far faster, tougher and cleverer than he looks. Ranger horses are bred and trained apart from other stock and will only accept a rider who knows the proper greeting.
characters.name: Tug

characters.description: Halt's former apprentice, now a Ranger with a fief of his own in the south. He is young, tall and good-humoured where Halt is dour, and unusual among Rangers in that he was also trained to the sword, which he uses better than most knights.
characters.name: Gilan

recaps.ending: Halt and Gilan corner the two Kalkara near the ruins of Morgarath's old castle at Gorlan. Ordinary arrows do almost nothing to them, and Halt's plan depends on fire. He brings one creature down, but the second reaches him, and the terror of its stare leaves him unable to move or shoot. Will, who was sent away with dispatches and disobeyed, arrives in time to set an arrow alight and put it into the creature, which burns and dies. Both Kalkara are destroyed and Halt and Gilan survive. Morgarath's attempt to murder Araluen's senior commanders before a war has failed, but the attempt itself tells the kingdom that he is preparing to move against it, and the fiefs begin arming. Back at Redmont, Will is publicly honoured for what he did, and Baron Arald offers him the place in Battleschool he wanted more than anything a few months earlier. Will refuses it: he is a Ranger's apprentice and intends to stay one. Halt, who is not given to praise, is plainly satisfied. Will's friendship with Horace, impossible at the start of the book, is settled, and the question of who his father was remains open.
recaps.in_short: Will, a slight, quick orphan raised as a ward of Castle Redmont in the kingdom of Araluen, wants a place in Battleschool and is refused as too small for it. Instead he is taken as apprentice by Halt, the fief's grim Ranger, and learns that the Rangers are not sorcerers but the King's scouts and intelligence corps, trained in concealment, tracking, the knife and the longbow. While Will learns the craft and makes an unlikely peace with Horace, an old tormentor now at Battleschool, the exiled rebel lord Morgarath sends two Kalkara, huge beasts whose stare paralyses with fear, to murder Araluen's senior commanders ahead of a war. Halt and his former apprentice Gilan track the creatures to the ruins of Morgarath's old castle at Gorlan. Halt kills one; when the second overpowers him, Will destroys it with a burning arrow. The kingdom's command survives, and Will, offered the Battleschool place he once longed for, chooses to remain a Ranger's apprentice as Araluen prepares for war.

recaps.text: In the kingdom of Araluen, five orphaned wards of Castle Redmont reach the age at which they are offered craft apprenticeships. Will, the smallest and quickest of them, has always wanted Battleschool, believing it the only way to live up to a father he was told died a soldier. At the Choosing, Baron Arald's Battlemaster Sir Rodney turns him down as too slight, while Horace, a big ward who has bullied Will for years, is accepted. Alyss is taken by the Diplomatic Service, Jenny by the kitchens and George by the scribes, leaving Will the only one unplaced. Halt, the fief's silent and widely feared Ranger, hands the Baron a note about Will, and Will finds himself apprenticed to him instead. Before this, the reader has seen the exiled rebel lord Morgarath in his mountain stronghold, deciding that the way to beat Araluen is to kill the men who would lead its army, and sending out two of his creatures to do it.

Will moves out of the castle to Halt's cottage at the edge of the forest and starts an apprenticeship nothing like the one he imagined. The Rangers turn out not to be sorcerers at all but the King's corps of scouts and intelligence gatherers, one to a fief, answerable to the King through their Commandant. Their reputation for magic is a useful side effect of what they actually do: move unseen in mottled cloaks, watch, and shoot better than anyone else in the kingdom. Halt teaches by setting tasks rather than explaining, and Will spends his days on unseen movement, on drawing a bow far heavier than he expected, and on knife work. He also learns that his old rival Horace is finding Battleschool much harder than he expected.

Will's training deepens: camouflage, silent movement, tracking, and constant archery practice. He is given a horse of his own, Tug, a small shaggy Ranger horse who is faster and cleverer than he looks and will not accept a rider who does not know the proper greeting. At Battleschool, Horace is being systematically bullied by three second-year cadets who make his life miserable and who he cannot report without appearing to whine. Will and Horace, thrown together on a boar hunt in which each of them ends up owing the other his safety, finally put down their old feud and become friends.

Lord Northolt, the most senior commander of the King's army, is found murdered, killed by something no ordinary man could have faced. Halt's former apprentice Gilan, now a Ranger in his own right and a rare swordsman among them, arrives at Redmont, and between them the Rangers identify what did it: the Kalkara, enormous half-legendary beasts that Morgarath keeps and that arrows barely touch. Halt concludes that Morgarath is picking off Araluen's commanders one by one in preparation for war, and that Baron Arald is on the list. Meanwhile the bullying at Battleschool comes into the open, and Horace faces the three older cadets and beats them, which ends their careers there and confirms how good he is going to be.

Rather than wait for the Kalkara to reach Redmont, Halt takes the hunt to them. He and Gilan ride out to intercept the creatures before they can reach their next target, working out where they must be heading and what might actually kill them, since arrows plainly will not. Will is sent away with messages and orders to stay clear of the pursuit, and Horace goes with him. Neither of them is willing to leave the two Rangers to face the creatures alone, and they follow the trail instead.

The hunt converges on the ruins of Castle Gorlan, Morgarath's own seat before his rebellion, now a wreck in a deserted fief. Halt and Gilan set their ambush there and discover how little effect their shooting has: arrows lodge in the creatures' hides without stopping them, and the fear a Kalkara's stare produces is close to physical, holding a man in place while it closes. Halt's answer is fire. Will and Horace, still following against orders, are close enough behind to see what the two Rangers are facing.

In the final confrontation Halt kills the first Kalkara, but the second reaches him and the terror of its gaze leaves him rooted and unable to shoot. Will arrives, sets an arrow burning and shoots the creature, which catches fire and dies. Both Kalkara are destroyed, and with them Morgarath's plan to behead the kingdom's command. The attempt has told Araluen what it needed to know, and the fiefs begin preparing for the war Morgarath clearly intends. At Redmont, Will is honoured for what he did, and Baron Arald offers him the Battleschool place he had wanted all his life. Will turns it down and stays Halt's apprentice, and his friendship with Horace, unthinkable a few months earlier, holds.

characters.description: Leader of the Twilight Melody sect and an Oblivion cultivator known as the Undying Void. He confronts the Herald of the Machine and insists that the latest human arrivals retain their freedom of choice.
characters.name: Ryun Nacht

characters.description: A Warden and time-aspect fighter who prevents a clash between Ryun and the Herald of the Machine over the latest human arrivals.
characters.name: Zacharia Gardner

characters.description: An unidentified Herald of the Machine who seeks custody of the survivors newly arrived from the Eighth Iteration.
characters.name: the Herald of the Machine

characters.description: Twilight Melody's principal administrator and sect leader. Anrosh manages the faction's growth and authorizes the costly, long-term reconstruction of Consequence.
characters.name: Anrosh

characters.description: A Twilight Melody powerhouse and spear fighter known publicly as the Daughter of Dawn and Death.
characters.name: Nayra

characters.description: Zach's true-linked partner and a shadow specialist.
characters.name: Naha

characters.description: A Twilight Melody powerhouse known publicly as the Gravity Titan. She is a partner of Ryun and Selia.
characters.name: Erdania

characters.description: Ryun and Erdania's absent partner. A faint bond assures Ryun that Selia still exists, but she has remained in the afterlife far longer than expected, leaving her partners waiting to advance and uncertain when she can return.
characters.name: Selia

characters.description: A senior Twilight Melody cultivator who is away with her partner and serves as an intermediary between major factions.
characters.name: Tali

characters.description: The adopted daughter of Anrosh and Nayra, a frontier commander, and Twilight Melody's designated heir. Her mentors delay her Immortal step until she settles on a suitable second aspect.
characters.name: Kri

characters.description: A young trainee guided jointly by Zach and Naha. His Legacy Shadowblade class emphasizes survival, shadow, and the blade, while his teachers encourage him to choose his next aspect for himself.
characters.name: the unnamed Warden trainee

characters.description: Ryun and Tali's new pupil, trained to adapt and survive even when deprived of his class powers.
characters.name: Hero

characters.description: An Unchained revolutionary who covertly observes the great factions' dome battles. Kael believes established powers and imposed social structures prevent genuine freedom, and he studies their abilities while working toward a radically remade world.
characters.name: Kael

characters.description: A commander who leads the costly assault on the Hellshoe dome. Greyhorde can amplify herself through a true link with her champion and isolate an opponent in a separate realm.
characters.name: Greyhorde

characters.description: An old-iteration runesmith whose early arrival falls outside the world's expected course. Ra'azel seeks access to the present Framework.
characters.name: Ra'azel

characters.description: The sentient voice within Zach's sword. Ravalim recognizes Ra'azel as a runesmith and gives Zach tactical advice during their battle.
characters.name: Ravalim

characters.description: A Twilight Melody specialist who designs and grows defensive and utility plants on the scale of an entire city.
characters.name: the Twilight Melody sect horticulturist

characters.description: An undead necromancer and accomplished crafter who rules a heavily fortified citadel. Eratemus possesses rare materials and a forge that Ryun seeks for his work.
characters.name: Eratemus

characters.description: A former slave and Unchained member with exceptional control of space. Kael secured his freedom and became his mentor, while the movement teaches liberation from coercive authority even at extreme human cost.
characters.name: the Minotaur spatial fighter

characters.description: Leader of a breakaway Grand Spirit faction that wants to pursue Ra'azel from the ethereal realm into the real realm.
characters.name: the Grand Spirit of War

characters.description: A former ally of the Grand Spirit of War who secretly approaches Ryun and Nayra with Mysteries to request help from a Chosen.
characters.name: the Grand Spirit of Transition

characters.description: A former ally of the Grand Spirit of War who secretly approaches Ryun and Nayra with Transition to request help from a Chosen.
characters.name: the Grand Spirit of Mysteries

characters.name: the Grand Spirit of Knowledge

characters.description: Tali's allied light-lance fighter. Sigmund supports her with spoken commands that reshape reality but exact a heavy personal toll.
characters.name: Sigmund

characters.name: the Golden Sky sect head

characters.description: Nayra's older brother and Eric's twin, whom she meets in the warrior afterlife.
characters.name: Nathan

characters.name: the Unchained leader

characters.name: the rescued Ravzur former League infiltrator

characters.name: Zenker

characters.name: Brightstar
